description: I'm building an interactive lunar survival game for NASA Space Apps. Looking for creative programmers, 3D designers, game developers and space enthusiasts who enjoy teamwork, innovation and turning ideas into reality. Let's create something amazing together!
summary:
**COSMIC OUTPOST: THE LAST 30 DAYS**

Cosmic Outpost is a 3D lunar exploration game designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of living on the Moon. Players take the role of an astronaut exploring a lunar environment using astronaut movement and a rover, while experiencing a simulated lunar research outpost.

The project aims to make space science more engaging by allowing players to explore a Moon-inspired environment and interact with a space-themed setting. It addresses the challenge of making complex space exploration concepts easier for children to understand through an interactive digital experience rather than traditional text-based learning.

The project represents an initial step towards combining space exploration, STEM education and game-based learning. Its goal is to inspire curiosity about lunar missions and help young learners develop an interest in the science and engineering required for future human exploration of the Moon.
details:
COSMIC OUTPOST: THE LAST 30 DAYS

Cosmic Outpost is a 3D browser-based lunar survival and exploration simulation designed to introduce children to the challenges of establishing a human presence on the Moon. Players take the role of a mission commander and manage a simulated lunar outpost through exploration, mission challenges and resource allocation.

The game features a 3D lunar environment, astronaut movement, a 360-degree camera, rover exploration, mission chapters and a resource management system. Players can monitor oxygen, water, food, electricity and radiation levels while learning why these resources are essential for astronaut survival.

The project also incorporates NASA-related scientific information from DONKI, OSDR and RadLab, including archived space-weather events, radiation research and space biology findings. Science explanations are adapted for different age groups to make complex concepts easier to understand.

Our goal is to make space science more engaging through interactive gameplay rather than traditional text-based learning. The project aims to encourage curiosity, scientific thinking and awareness of the engineering challenges involved in future lunar exploration.

Technologies used: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js and WebGL. The project was developed as a browser-based application without requiring additional hardware.

Creativity lies in combining lunar exploration, survival simulation and age-adapted STEM learning in one interactive experience.
